GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2025-03-27T17:21:20Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Issue with incomplete pip installation - macOS
Description: Description:
I'm encountering an issue when trying to install the openai-agents package. After a successful installation via pip, the package seems to be incomplete — the openai_agents directory in site-packages only contains metadata files (INSTALLER, METADATA, RECORD, etc.), with no actual Python module files. As a result, I cannot import the module, and attempts to do so result in a ModuleNotFoundError.

Steps to Reproduce:
Create a fresh Python environment:

bash
Copy
python3 -m venv env
Activate the environment:

bash
Copy
source env/bin/activate
Install openai-agents:

bash
Copy
pip install openai-agents
After installation, run the following to verify the installation:

bash
Copy
pip show openai-agents
The output shows the installation is successful, but the site-packages/openai_agents directory contains only metadata files.

Attempt to import the module in Python:

python
Copy
from openai_agents import Agent
This results in a ModuleNotFoundError.

Expected Behavior:
The openai-agents package should include the necessary Python modules under the site-packages/openai_agents directory. I should be able to import the module as follows:

python
Copy
from openai_agents import Agent
Actual Behavior:
After installation, the site-packages/openai_agents directory contains only metadata files (INSTALLER, METADATA, RECORD, etc.), and the Python modules (openai_agents/__init__.py, etc.) are missing. Consequently, I am unable to import the module.

Environment:
Python version: 3.9.6

Operating System: macOS 11.0

Package version: openai-agents 0.0.7

Installation method: pip install openai-agents

Additional Information:
I’ve tried reinstalling the package multiple times using --no-cache-dir and have also used a fresh virtual environment.

I have also checked the site-packages/openai_agents directory, and it is missing the necessary Python files.

I’ve checked the PyPI page, and there’s no indication of a known issue with the package installation.

The issue persists after upgrading pip to the latest version.
